title: Formal smoothness lifts along a flat map over a square-zero ideal
statement: Let $\varphi:R\to S$ be a homomorphism of commutative rings, making $S$ an $R$-algebra, and let $I\subseteq R$ be an ideal; write $IS$ for the ideal of $S$ generated by $\varphi(I)$, and $\bar\varphi:R/I\to S/IS$ for the ring map induced by $\varphi$, making $S/IS$ an $R/I$-algebra. Assume (1) $I^2=0$; (2) $S$ is a flat $R$-module via $\varphi$ [def-weil-pbc-flat-ring-map]; (3) $\bar\varphi$ is formally smooth (the case $\mathfrak n=0$ of [def-weil-pbc-formally-smooth-adic]): for every commutative ring $D$ with a ring map $R/I\to D$, every ideal $J\subseteq D$ with $J^2=0$, with quotient map $q:D\to D/J$ [def-weil-pbc-algebra-hom-quotient], and every homomorphism of $R/I$-algebras $g:S/IS\to D/J$, there is a homomorphism of $R/I$-algebras $f:S/IS\to D$ with $q\circ f=g$. Then $\varphi$ is formally smooth (the case $\mathfrak n=0$ of [def-weil-pbc-formally-smooth-adic]): for every commutative ring $D$ with a ring map $R\to D$, every ideal $J\subseteq D$ with $J^2=0$, with quotient map $q:D\to D/J$, and every homomorphism of $R$-algebras $g:S\to D/J$, there is a homomorphism of $R$-algebras $f:S\to D$ with $q\circ f=g$.
